result.title: Advancing Entropy-Level Credit Assignment in RLVR via Proximal Entropy Policy Optimization
result.summary: Value-model-free RLVR methods such as GRPO assign uniform advantages to all tokens in a rollout, ignoring that tokens contribute unequally. Recent methods use token entropy as an importance proxy but compute it globally across the batch, conflating importance with prompt difficulty and positional trends. We argue that importance should instead be measured relative to the local context of each token. We introduce proximal entropy, a local measure of token importance relative to neighboring tokens, and prove it is invariant to both confounders. Proximal Entropy Policy Optimization (PEPO) uses it to weight per-token advantages and outperforms GRPO and entropy-based baselines on mathematical reasoning across Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B, and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct. We also show the formulation generalizes to other algorithms where substituting proximal entropy into existing methods improves, and applying it to single-stream RL succeeds where global entropy fails.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 proximal entropy（局部熵）作为 token 重要性的度量，并据此设计 PEPO，用局部上下文相关的熵对每个 token 的 advantage 加权，在多个模型上改善数学推理的 RLVR 训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 它给出按局部上下文而非全局批次计算 token 重要性的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中贡献分配与监督（哪些 token/片段真正驱动答案）以及视觉与文本 token 重要性差异的问题，但研究对象是纯文本 RLVR，需人工判断能否迁移到多模态 latent 状态。
